subject: SLA windowing & probe concordance - instrumentation workshop follow-up

Subject: Follow-up: SLA windowing / probe concordance workshop

Sofia / team —

Thanks again for running the workshop this morning. Our procurement and SRE teams found the session useful but we have a few follow-ups before we sign off on the SLA amendment:

1) Windowing definition: we need a clear example of how regional partial degradations are aggregated into a single monthly availability calculation. Please include the exact formula, the time buckets, and whether synthetic probes are weighted differently from real-traffic telemetry.

2) Probe concordance: Atlas runs two independent synthetic probe fleets (internal and partner probes). We need to understand how Redwood will reconcile divergent probe readings and what evidence you will accept if probes disagree (e.g., partner probe shows 99.95% while Redwood’s global probes show 99.6%).

3) Clock sync and latency attribution: provide the expected clock skew tolerance and any compensation method (NTP drift assumptions) you use when attributing on-the-wire latency to Redwood versus client-side network.

4) Evidence package: list of artifacts we should expect monthly for audit (time-series tsv/csv, aggregated percentile tables, sampling queries, and a short narrative). If you can, include a short sample dataset.

Can you please respond with a consolidated approach and an initial draft of the amendment (so our legal team has text to review)? Also, please attach any workshop slides or playbook drafts you referenced.

Thanks — looking to close this week if possible.

Claire Hammond

Claire —

Appreciate the quick recap. Attached is a first-pass playbook (instrumentation_playbook_v1.pdf) and the slide deck from the workshop. High level answers below; Karthik will add measurement details.

1) Windowing aggregation (summary):
- We compute availability per-region using minute-level buckets (60s) and then aggregate to hourly and daily windows. Monthly availability is the weighted average of regional hourly availabilities, weighted by accepted production traffic (not synthetic probes).
- Partial regional degradations are treated as "partial outages" where the region's contribution is scaled by observed successful request fraction; the formula and a worked example are in section 3 of the playbook.

2) Probe concordance (summary):
- We classify probe sources into three tiers: Redwood-global, Customer-owned (if you run your probes from inside Atlas network), and Partner probes. Concordance is evaluated at 1-minute granularity.
- If customer-owned and Redwood-global disagree by >0.5% failure rate over a 15-minute sliding window, we trigger a concordance review and collect raw request/response logs for that window. The acceptance rules and escalation steps are in the playbook appendix.

3) Clock sync:
- Redwood requires NTP-synced hosts with drift <200ms for probe and telemetry collectors. For attribution we apply a +/-200ms tolerance and align time-series using server timestamps; when client-side RTT is dominant we annotate the sample rather than reassigning blame.

4) Evidence package:
- Monthly package includes: raw probe CSVs (per-minute), aggregated p50/p90/p99 latency tables, availability tables (per-region, per-hour), sampling queries used, and a short narrative describing any exceptions. Example files are included in the attached probe-mapping.csv and the playbook.

Next steps: Karthik will outline the exact percentile definitions and the sampling queries we will publish as part of the amendment. We will also upload a sample time-series to the Drive link below. Draft amendment (sla_amendment_draft.docx) is attached for legal review — it contains the measurement language we recommend.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-example-link

If this looks OK, I can coordinate a short legal-to-legal redline session tomorrow.

—Sofia

Subject: Re: Follow-up: SLA windowing / probe concordance workshop

Claire / Sofia / team —

Adding the measurement specifics we discussed. Below are the operational rules and the sample queries we will publish with the amendment.

Operational rules (concise):
- Bucket size: 60s minute buckets for probes and server-side telemetry.
- Failure definition: a probe is a "failure" if HTTP 5xx OR (latency > 10s) OR (TLS handshake error).
- Regional availability: region_avail_hour = 1 - (failed_requests_in_hour / total_requests_in_hour) using only production traffic. Synthetic probes are used for detection and evidence but not for weighting availability unless explicitly accepted in writing.
- Concordance: we compute pairwise failure-rate delta across sources at 1-min granularity. If delta > 0.5% for a 15-min sliding window AND production request error rate corroborates, we mark as service-impacting for attribution. If delta is > 2% but production traffic does not corroborate, we mark as "probe divergence" and open an investigation but not an automatic credit.

Sampling queries (examples):
- Raw probe export (CSV): SELECT time_bucket('1 minute', ts) AS minute, source, sum(case when is_failure then 1 else 0 end) as failures, count(*) as total FROM probes WHERE service = 'redwood-inference' AND acct = 'ATL-4283' AND ts >= $start AND ts < $end GROUP BY minute, source ORDER BY minute;
- Latency aggregation: select minute, percentile_cont(0.50) within group (order by rtt) as p50, percentile_cont(0.95) as p95, percentile_cont(0.99) as p99 from server_requests where acct='ATL-4283' and ts between $start and $end group by minute;

Evidence retention and delivery:
- We will retain raw probe logs for 90 days and aggregated monthly artifacts for 13 months for audit. Monthly evidence bundle will be uploaded to the shared Drive folder by the 5th business day and will include: per-minute CSVs (zipped), an aggregated metrics CSV, and a short notes.txt with any anomalies noted.

Attached: probe-mapping.csv (sample mapping of probe sources to regions) and a one-page sample output (we will upload a larger time-series to Drive tonight).

Edge cases: for cross-region partial degradations where we see <1% of total traffic affected but a single region reports >5% failure rate, we will follow the concordance path above and present both raw and aggregated data to Atlas to jointly decide crediting. The amendment contains an arbitration clause for unresolved disputes.

Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through any of the SQLs.

-Karthik
Principal Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
